Subject: Private deploy visibility: export options & SIEM onboarding

Hi Avery,

Thanks for taking this on. We're getting close to provisioning the Arcadia VPC tenant for Redwood Private. Before we flip any routes over, Security wants clarity on how observability data will leave our environment for ingestion into our Splunk instance and for long-term retention for audits. Specific asks:

- What export modes do you support from the private control plane and inference nodes (push, pull, forwarder)?
- Do you have a recommended pattern for customers that cannot accept outbound TLS connections to third-party endpoints (i.e., must push to an S3 bucket in our account and have our SIEM pull)?
- How are trace hooks injected for request correlation? We need a short, copyable code snippet and an estimate of overhead (p50/p99 added latency).
- Encryption in transit and at rest for exported artifacts, and how we can prove chain-of-custody for SOC2 auditors.

We also have firewall rules that only allow outbound 443 to a small list of IPs; can you provide the endpoints and IP ranges we need to approve?

If it's helpful we can hop on a quick 30-minute call next week.

Thanks —
John
John Patel
Director, Platform Security
Arcadia Health

John —

Appreciate the clear list. High level answers below and I attached a short architecture doc with patterns and the tracehook example. Please see the attached PDF (redwood-private-export-patterns-v1.pdf) and a small patch with the tracehook snippet (tracehook-example.patch).

Short answers:
- Supported export modes: 1) Push-forwarder (agent in your VPC -> our collector or your S3), 2) Customer-pull (our control plane writes to a customer-owned S3 or storage and you pull), 3) Relay via an approved SIEM endpoint (HEC). We prefer push-forwarder when latency-sensitive and pull when egress restrictions are strict.

- For egress-restricted customers: recommended pattern is customer-owned S3 with presigned object upload from the forwarder, or an on-prem relay that you run inside the tenant which writes to your internal SIEM. We document ACLs and lifecycle policy in the PDF.

- Trace hooks: lightweight header-based correlation (x-rw-trace-id, x-rw-span). The attached patch shows the minimal instrumentation to add to your API gateway. Overhead: typical P50 additional processing is <0.5ms, P99 ~2.5ms depending on sampling and pipeline. We'll include benchmark numbers for your exact deployment once we have CPU/GPU sizing.

- Encryption & chain-of-custody: all exported payloads are TLS 1.3; when writing to a customer S3 we recommend SSE-KMS with your key (we support KMS key IDs). For transfers from the forwarder to Redwood collectors we use mTLS and we log certificate IDs. For audit evidence we provide signed manifests and a runbook describing the export timestamps and checksums (see attachment).

- Endpoints/IPs: for the minimal allowlist you can open outbound 443 to our customer relay ELB (range documented in the PDF). If you need an exact prefix list for firewall, we can provide a short-lived set during onboarding and rotate monthly — we do not publish a static global IP list.

Next steps I propose:
1) Review the attached patterns doc and the tracehook snippet.
2) Kimberly and Marcus to propose the SOC2 evidence matrix mapping.
3) Short call Wed or Thu to walk through the S3/presigned flow and test a one-time export.

I copied Kim and Marcus to align on the compliance checklist — Kim, Marcus, any immediate red flags?

Best,
Avery Johnson
Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks Avery, and hi John —

I went through the PDF and want to call out a few things the SOC2 reviewers will look for. I put a quick mapping into an attachment (soc2-evidence-mapping.xlsx) but the highlights are below:

- Authentication & key custody: If Arcadia uses SSE-KMS, please provide the KMS key ARN and rotation cadence. We will include signed KMS usage logs in the evidence bundle.
- Immutable manifests: enable manifest signing on export; manifests should include SHA256 checksums per object and a timestamp. We'll sign with our export certificate and include cert serials in the audit package.
- Network controls: instead of a wide IP allowlist, we recommend a short-lived CIDR block approach for the onboarding window, plus mTLS with client cert pinning on your forwarder. This gives auditors proof of constrained egress.
- Retention mapping: we need to confirm which logs are considered user-data vs operational telemetry. Operational telemetry we retain 90 days by default; customer evidence exports can be configured to your retention policy.

Also: sample rate for traces — we recommend deterministic sampling on error paths + adaptive sampling to keep telemetry volume bounded. The tracehook we provided supports sampling flags so you can mark high-cardinality traces for capture.

Proposed immediate deliverables from Redwood:
- A short one-page export runbook tailored to Arcadia (we'll produce this if you confirm the S3 vs HEC path).
- A signed manifest sample and a small test object that you can verify in your environment.
- A mapping table that ties exported artifacts to SOC2 control IDs (see attached).

John — if you can confirm whether you'd prefer S3 (customer-owned) or direct HEC push, we'll prioritize the runbook. Also, please share the mail alias used by your auditors (if they need direct access to sample artifacts).

Kimberly Park
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
